title: Poetry: solving conflicts and appreciating a poem
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Stories and poems often show a problem between people — a conflict. A thoughtful reader can suggest a fair solution, and can say why a poem is worth enjoying.
A conflict is a problem between characters. A good solution is fair to everyone involved.
Read this: 'Two friends, Amir and Jed, both want to ride the one bicycle at the same time.'

blocks.question: What is the fairest solution to their conflict?
options: One friend keeps it all day.
blocks.explain: Taking turns is fair to both friends, so it is the best solution.
blocks.rule: A good solution to a conflict is fair to everyone involved.

practiceItems.prompt: a problem between characters is called a ___
a fair way to share one bike between two friends is to take ___
a good solution is ___ to everyone (fair/unfair)
solving a conflict means finding a fair ___

blocks.content: To appreciate a poem is to say what you enjoyed about it and why — its images, its sounds, or its message.

blocks.question: Which shows real appreciation of a poem?
options: I liked how the sea images made me feel calm.
blocks.explain: It names what was enjoyed (the sea images) and the effect (feeling calm) — that is appreciation.
blocks.rule: Appreciating a poem means saying what you enjoyed and why.

practiceItems.prompt: saying why you enjoyed a poem shows ___ (appreciation/anger)
appreciation should say what you enjoyed and ___
a fair fix to a problem is a good ___
a problem between characters is a ___

blocks.content: Suggest solutions that are fair to all, and say clearly why a poem is worth enjoying. Let's practise!
